# Run, back up and package the hub

## Intent

An operator must be able to trust the hub as a thing that is run: it refuses to start on a host that cannot serve git, it opens the data an earlier release wrote, its logs can be fed to a machine and never leak a credential, a backup taken while it works restores to a hub that starts, it ships as images and manifests that run it the one supported way, and its performance targets are measured rather than assumed. This package delivers those guarantees of the non-functional requirements that no feature package owns.

## Goals

- `parleyd` runs `git --version` once at every serving start and refuses to start (exit status 1, one error line) when `git` is missing, older than 2.38 or does not answer.
- A recorded data directory of each release is kept in the repository, and a test starts the current binary on each one: the missing schema steps are applied, the recorded ones are kept, the repositories are still read by stock `git`, and a second start applies nothing.
- Every log line is one JSON object with `time`, `level` and `msg`; a line written while a request is handled carries that request's `request_id`; no attribute of any type and no query string carries a credential into the log.
- A snapshot written by `parleyd backup` while writers commit transactions and git clients push is copied to a new place and a hub started on the copy starts, answers `GET /readyz` with 200 and accepts new work; its stores pass an integrity check and its repositories pass `git fsck`.
- A hub container image runs `parleyd` as a non-root user with its configuration and data on one volume; a reference sandbox image holds `git` and the `parley` CLI; Kubernetes manifests run the hub image with exactly one replica on a persistent volume.
- `go test ./test/perf/` with `PARLEY_PERF_URL` set measures the fourteen targets of §15.4 against a running hub and writes a JSON report that says, per target, the measured value and whether the target was met. Without that variable the test is skipped, and a missed target never fails a test run.

This package tests and extends them and does not specify them again.

That the line's `path` holds no query string is package 02's criterion too (REQ-8.5 there); this package relies on it and changes nothing in `internal/server/accesslog.go` (Design Decision 20). The level names of Design Decision 8 are written by package 03's logger in `internal/hub/logging.go`, which this package extends.
- The two binaries, the build values set by the linker and their report by `GET /version` and `parley version` (NFR-005, the binaries of NFR-006, NFR-041): package 01 hub_skeleton.
- No lock that a request waits on, and compare-and-swap of refs (NFR-010): packages 18 git_push_rules, 21 scm_write_api and 25 optimistic_landing. The exclusive periods of clone, reclone, archive and delete: packages 10 workspace_create_and_clone and 14 workspace_archive_reclone_delete.
- Readers never see a partial update (NFR-011) and state that must agree changes atomically (NFR-012): packages 18 git_push_rules, 22 change_opening_and_versions, 25 optimistic_landing, 34 rebuild_execution and 52 durable_event_log_and_stream.
- Background work survives a restart, and refs are reconciled with records at start (NFR-013): packages 10 workspace_create_and_clone, 23 change_lifecycle_and_mergeability, 24 change_stacks_and_restack, 25 optimistic_landing, 29 auto_land_revert_and_path_limits, 33 rebuild_jobs and 45 sandbox_creation_and_credentials, each as a start hook of package 03. This package shows only that those hooks run on restored data.

- Security requirements NFR-020 to NFR-028 and NFR-044: packages 39 secrets and 06 api_keys_and_access_tokens (NFR-020), 03 (NFR-021), 07 workspace_access_rule and 17 git_smart_http (NFR-022), 17 and 18 (NFR-023), 06 and 08 workspace_bound_tokens (NFR-024), 43 forge_webhook_ingress (NFR-025), 18, 21 and 25 (NFR-026), 45 sandbox_creation_and_credentials and 48 sandbox_network_policy (NFR-027, NFR-028), 53 event_webhooks (NFR-044).

## Background

The repository holds no code yet; every file named here is new. The source is `docs/prd/15_non_functional.md`. Most of its requirements restate guarantees that feature sections own; the Non-goals name the owner of each. What is left for this package is the part of §15 that is about running the product:

- NFR-004: "The server needs the `git` command at run time (version 2.38 or later, checked at start)."
- NFR-003: "a newer binary can always open the data of the previous release."
- NFR-042: "Logs are structured (one JSON object per line), carry the request id, and never contain credentials or secret values."
- NFR-007: "A hub started on a restored snapshot starts cleanly."
- NFR-006: a hub container image, a reference sandbox image that satisfies the image contract of §13.9, and Kubernetes manifests.

Package 03 delivers what this package builds on: the run function of the hub in `internal/hub/` (it takes the arguments, an environment lookup, the working directory, stdout and stderr and returns the exit status), start hooks that run in registration order before the listener is bound, the rule that a failing start exits 1 with one JSON error line, the stores with their schema steps in `internal/store/`, the logger in `internal/hub/logging.go` that applies the scrubber of `internal/scrub/`, and `parleyd backup`. Package 02 delivers the request id and the access-log line in `internal/server/`.

This package builds in these places:

## Requirements

### The `git` version check at start (NFR-004)

When `parleyd` starts to serve, it runs `git --version` once. The check is the first start hook, named `git-version`: it runs after the configuration is loaded, the data is opened and the bootstrap has run, and before every other start hook, so no hook ever runs `git` on a host where the check would fail. `git` is looked up on the `PATH` of the environment the hub was started with.

The first line of the output must have the form `git version <major>.<minor>` followed by anything: `git version 2.38.0`, `git version 2.39.3 (Apple Git-146)`, `git version 2.45.1.windows.1` and `git version 2.50.0-rc1` are all read. The version is accepted when (major, minor) is at least (2, 38): 2.38.0 is accepted, 2.37.7 is refused, 3.0 is accepted. On success the hub writes one info log line with `msg` `git version checked` and the member `git_version` holding the text after `git version ` up to the first space.

Failures stop the start as every failing start hook does (exit status 1, one JSON error line on stderr, no `listening` line, no later hook called). The error line's text contains:

| Case | Text |
|---|---|
| no `git` on `PATH` | `git not found on PATH; parleyd needs git 2.38 or later` |
| version below 2.38 | `git <found> is too old; parleyd needs git 2.38 or later` |
| first line not of the form above | `cannot read the git version from "<first line, cut to 100 bytes>"` |
| `git --version` exits with a status other than 0 | `git --version failed: exit status <n>` |
| no answer within 10 seconds | `git --version failed: no answer within 10s`; the `git` process is killed |

Runs that do not serve do not run `git`: `parleyd --help`, a usage error, `parleyd backup <directory>`, and a bootstrap run that writes the admin token and exits (`--admin-email` on a new hub, `--reset-admin-token`). They behave the same on a host without `git`.

### Opening the previous release's data (NFR-003)

**Recorded data.** `go run ./test/upgrade/record <name>` records the data of the binary it is built from. It starts a hub in a temporary directory with `--admin-email`, starts it again to serve, creates one bare repository `fixture.git` with one commit on `main` under the workspace root, stops the hub with a clean shutdown, and writes `test/upgrade/testdata/<name>.tar.gz`. The archive holds the data directory (the transactional store, the analytical store, the workspace root) and `manifest.json`:

```json
{"release":"<name>","recorded_at":"<timestamp>",
 "steps":{"transactional":["<step>", "..."],"analytical":["<step>", "..."]},
 "admin_token_sha256":"<64 hex>",
 "repositories":[{"path":"fixture.git","refs":{"refs/heads/main":"<40 hex>"}}]}
```

`steps` lists the schema steps each store records as applied, in the order they were applied. `<name>` matches `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,62}$`. The recorder exits 0 and prints the archive's path. It exits 1, with one line on stderr and nothing written or changed, when the name does not match or the archive already exists. The archive `baseline.tar.gz` is recorded when this package is implemented; one archive is recorded and committed at each release, named after the release. Archives older than the previous release may be deleted.

**The guarantee.** For every archive under `test/upgrade/testdata/`, a hub started on the unpacked data with no flags:

- applies every registered schema step the data does not record and no recorded one, logs the `listening` line and answers `GET /readyz` with 200;
- records, in each store, a list of applied steps that begins with the manifest's list for that store in the same order;
- still holds the admin token hash of the manifest;
- leaves each repository readable by stock `git`: `git fsck` succeeds and each ref of the manifest resolves to the commit id of the manifest;
- stops with exit status 0 on SIGTERM, and when started again applies no step and leaves both lists of applied steps as they were.

**The compatibility rule.** Data can be opened only if the binary still knows what the data records. A list of recorded steps is compatible with a list of registered steps when every recorded name is registered and the recorded names appear among the registered ones in the same relative order. The upgrade test applies this rule to every archive before it starts the hub and fails naming the first step that breaks it; so renaming, removing or reordering a released schema step fails the ordinary test run.

### Structured logging (NFR-042)

Package 03 writes every line as one JSON object on stderr, filters by level and passes the message and string attributes through the scrubber. This package fixes the rest.

**Members of every line.** `time` is an RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC ending in `Z`. `level` is one of `TRACE`, `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARN`, `ERROR`. `msg` is a string. A line is exactly one line: a line break inside a message or a value appears escaped.

**The request id.** A line logged with the context of a request carries the member `request_id`, equal to the `X-Request-ID` header of that request's response. This holds for lines written by a handler, by a middleware and by code a handler calls with the request's context. A line logged outside a request (start, start hooks, the maintenance loop, background work) has no `request_id` member.

**Values of every type are scrubbed.** An attribute whose value is an error, a nested group of attributes, a list, a map, a byte slice or any value that is rendered as text is scrubbed like a string attribute: after rendering, no string in the line holds a registered secret value, a hub credential or user information in a URL. An error is rendered as its message. Numbers, booleans and durations are written unchanged.

**No query string.** The `path` member of the access-log line is the path of the request's URL without the query string, so a token passed as a query parameter (the forge ingress accepts one, §12) does not reach the log.

**A failing log write does not fail the hub.** When a write to stderr returns an error, the line is dropped; the request that caused it is answered as it would have been and the process keeps running.

**The audit.** A hub that runs at level `trace` and receives requests that carry marker secrets in an `Authorization: Bearer` header, in an `Authorization: Basic` header, in a `Cookie` header, in a JSON body and in a query parameter writes a log in which every line has the three members above, every access-log line has the `request_id` of its response, and no marker appears.

### Restoring a backup taken under load (NFR-007)

**Restoring** is copying: the operator copies the snapshot's transactional store to `[database].path`, its `analytics.db` beside it and its workspace directory to `[workspace].path` on the new host, puts the configuration file in place and starts `parleyd` with no flags. The snapshot holds no configuration directory; the configuration file is the operator's to keep.

A hub started on such a copy starts cleanly: it applies no schema step, runs every registered start hook to completion with the restored data open, logs the `listening` line and answers `GET /readyz` with 200. It still holds the admin token hash of the source hub. It accepts new work: a transaction commits and a push to a restored repository is accepted by stock `git`. The snapshot directory that was copied from is unchanged by all of this.

This holds for any snapshot taken under load, where load means at least four writers committing transactions to the transactional store, one writer committing to the analytical store and two git clients pushing new commits to two repositories under the workspace root for the whole duration of the backup:

- during the backup no writer's commit and no push returns an error;
- `PRAGMA integrity_check` answers `ok` on each restored store;
- `git fsck` succeeds on each restored repository, and each of its refs resolves to a commit that is the source repository's commit of that ref at the end of the load or an ancestor of it;
- every commit that was pushed before the backup started is reachable from the restored ref.

### The hub container image (NFR-006)

`containers/hub/Dockerfile`, built with the repository root as its context and the build arguments `VERSION`, `COMMIT` and `BUILD_TIME`, gives an image that:

- contains `parleyd` and `parley` in `/usr/local/bin`, both built without cgo and with the three build values set, and a `git` of version 2.38 or later;
- runs as the user and group id 10001, never as root;
- sets `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/var/lib/parley/config` and `XDG_DATA_HOME=/var/lib/parley/data`, declares `/var/lib/parley` as a volume and uses it as working directory, so that the configuration file, the admin token file, both stores and the repositories live on one volume;
- declares port 8080 and has the entry point `parleyd` in exec form, so that arguments of the container are arguments of `parleyd` and a stop signal reaches it.

A container started from the image with no arguments and an empty volume listens on port 8080, answers `GET /readyz` with 200, reports the build argument `VERSION` in `GET /version`, and has created `data/parley.db` on the volume as user 10001. When the container is stopped, `parleyd` exits with status 0 within 30 seconds. `parley version` run in the image prints the same `VERSION` as the client's version. `backup /var/lib/parley/snapshot` as the container's arguments, on the volume of a running hub, writes a snapshot and exits 0.

### The reference sandbox image (NFR-006, §13.9 image contract)

The image contract of §13.9: "A profile's image must contain `git` for the checkout and for checkpoints. Nothing else is required: no agent, no Parley component. An image that also contains the `parley` CLI can use it as it is."

`containers/sandbox/Dockerfile`, built like the hub image, gives the reference image. It contains `git` (2.38 or later), a POSIX shell at `/bin/sh`, the CA certificates of its base image and the `parley` CLI in `/usr/local/bin`. It contains no agent and no `parleyd`. It has no entry point, so the command the runtime starts runs unchanged, and its default user is not root (user id 1000, with a writable home directory).

The image tests hold a **contract check** that takes any image reference: as the image's default user, in a writable directory, `git init`, a commit and `git rev-parse HEAD` succeed. The tests run it against the reference image and, when `PARLEY_SANDBOX_IMAGE` is set, against that image too, so an operator can check an image of their own.

**Running the image tests.** The tests in `test/image/` need a container engine. They are skipped unless `PARLEY_IMAGE_TESTS=1`; the engine is the command named by `PARLEY_CONTAINER_ENGINE`, default `docker`. With `PARLEY_IMAGE_TESTS=1` and no such command they fail naming the command.

### Kubernetes manifests (NFR-006, NFR-001)

`deploy/kubernetes/` holds five files, every object named `parley` unless said otherwise and labelled `app.kubernetes.io/name: parley`:

| File | Object |
|---|---|
| `configmap.yaml` | a ConfigMap with one key, `config.toml` |
| `secret.example.yaml` | a Secret `parley-secrets` whose every value is the placeholder `replace-me` |
| `pvc.yaml` | a PersistentVolumeClaim `parley-data`, access mode `ReadWriteOnce`, 20Gi, no storage class named |
| `deployment.yaml` | a Deployment running the hub image |
| `service.yaml` | a Service of type `ClusterIP`, port 8080 to the container's port 8080 |

- **One process.** The Deployment has `replicas: 1` and the strategy `Recreate`, so that an update stops the old hub before it starts the new one and two hubs never open one data directory (NFR-001).
- **Storage.** The claim is mounted at `/var/lib/parley`. The ConfigMap's `config.toml` is mounted as the single file `/var/lib/parley/config/config.toml` (a `subPath` mount), which leaves the config dir on the volume and writable for the admin token file. The pod runs as user 10001, refuses to run as root, and sets `fsGroup: 10001`.
- **Configuration and secrets.** The Secret reaches the container as environment variables (`envFrom`). The `config.toml` of the ConfigMap is accepted by the hub's configuration loader when the environment holds the keys of the example Secret, and every `${NAME}` it uses is a key of the example Secret. It shows one OAuth provider whose `client_secret` is `${GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET}`.
- **Probes, port and stop.** The container's liveness probe is `GET /healthz` and its readiness probe `GET /readyz`, both on port 8080. The Service selects the pod's labels. `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` is 40, above the 30 seconds within which the hub exits after SIGTERM (PLAT-FR-004).

### The performance harness (§15.4)

**Running it.** `test/perf/` holds a harness that is a client of one running hub. The operator runs:

```sh
PARLEY_PERF_URL=https://hub.example PARLEY_PERF_TOKEN=... PARLEY_PERF_WORKSPACE=acme-app \
  go test ./test/perf/ -run TestPerformanceTargets -count=1 -timeout 3h -v
```

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `PARLEY_PERF_URL` | the hub's base URL. Unset: `TestPerformanceTargets` is skipped, with a message naming the variable |
| `PARLEY_PERF_TOKEN` | a user's credential with write access to the workspaces |
| `PARLEY_PERF_WORKSPACE` | one or more slugs of cloned workspaces, separated by commas. The first is used by every scenario; the others only by `active_forks` |
| `PARLEY_PERF_SANDBOX_PROFILE` | a sandbox profile. Unset: the three sandbox scenarios are `skipped` |
| `PARLEY_PERF_CAPACITY` | `1` runs the four capacity scenarios. Otherwise they are `skipped` |
| `PARLEY_PERF_REPORT` | where the report is written; default `parley-perf-report.json` in the system's temporary directory |

In the ordinary test run (`go test ./... -count=1`) no variable is set and the test is skipped; the harness's own logic (percentiles, verdicts, the report, the scenario runner) is tested there against a stub hub.

With `PARLEY_PERF_URL` set, the test fails only when the harness cannot do its job: `PARLEY_PERF_TOKEN` or `PARLEY_PERF_WORKSPACE` is unset (the message names the variable), `GET /version` does not answer 200 within 10 seconds, or the report cannot be written. A target that is missed, a scenario that is skipped and a scenario that ends in an error never fail the test.

**Scenarios.** Fourteen, one per row of §15.4, run one after the other in this order:

| Name | What is done | Measured | Target |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fork_create` | 50 forks created one after the other (`POST /workspaces/:slug/forks`) | p95 of the request duration, ms | under 1000 |
| `file_read` | 200 reads, alternately one file and one tree (`GET …/scm/file`, `GET …/scm/tree`) | p95, ms | under 100 |
| `commit_create` | 50 commits of 100 files each on a fork (`POST …/scm/commits`) | p95, ms | under 500 |
| `land` | 20 changes of 20 commits each with disjoint files, landed one at a time | p95 of the time from the land request to the land attempt's success, ms | under 2000 |
| `land_throughput` | 120 one-commit changes with disjoint files landed on one target branch, at most 8 land requests in flight | changes landed × 60 ÷ seconds elapsed | at least 60 |
| `land_concurrency` | 16 land requests for 16 non-conflicting changes sent at the same time | land attempts that did not end in success | at most 0 |
| `mergeability` | 100 open changes; the target branch is moved by landing one more change | seconds until none of the 100 reports `mergeable` `unknown` | at most 60 |
| `event_latency` | a subscriber on `GET /events`; 50 commits created one after the other | the largest time from a commit's response to the arrival of its event, ms | at most 1000 |
| `active_forks` (capacity) | forks created over all listed workspaces until 5,000 exist or the hub refuses | forks that exist at once | at least 5000 |
| `open_changes` (capacity) | changes opened in the first workspace until 2,000 are open or the hub refuses | open changes | at least 2000 |
| `event_streams` (capacity) | `GET /events` connections opened until 500 are open or the hub refuses | connections open at once | at least 500 |
| `sandboxes_running` (capacity, sandbox) | sandboxes created until 200 are `provisioning` or `ready` or the hub refuses | sandboxes in those states | at least 200 |
| `sandbox_ready` (sandbox) | 5 sandboxes created one after the other | the largest time from the create response to state `ready`, s | at most 60 |
| `sandbox_exec` (sandbox) | 50 execs of the command `true` in one sandbox | p95 of the request duration, ms; an upper bound of the hub's overhead | under 200 |

p95 is the nearest-rank percentile: of n samples sorted ascending, the one at position ⌈0.95·n⌉. A scenario that collected no sample has no measurement.

**Verdict of a scenario.** `met` when the measured value satisfies the target; `missed` when it does not; `skipped` when its variable is not set (the detail names the variable); `error` when a request that is not the scenario's expected stop is answered with a status of 400 or more or fails in transport, or when the scenario runs past its deadline (10 minutes; 60 minutes for a capacity scenario). The detail of an `error` names the method, the path, the status and the `error_type` of the first failing request, or says `deadline exceeded`. For a capacity scenario a refusal by the hub is the expected stop: the scenario ends, the count reached is the measurement and the detail holds the refusal's `error_type`. A scenario that ends in `error` does not stop the run; the next scenario runs.

**The harness leaves no work behind.** It never targets a workspace's default branch: it creates a target branch `perf/<run id>` and forks of its own. When a scenario ends, in any verdict, the harness deletes the forks and sandboxes that scenario created and closes its connections; a clean-up request that fails is listed in the report and changes no verdict.

**The report.** One JSON document, written to the report path and logged as a table by the test:

```json
{"hub":{"url":"https://hub.example","version":{"version":"1.4.0","commit":"3f2a1bc"}},
 "run_id":"<12 hex>","started_at":"<timestamp>","finished_at":"<timestamp>",
 "results":[{"name":"fork_create","target":{"comparison":"lt","value":1000,"unit":"ms"},
   "measured":412.5,"samples":50,"status":"met","detail":""}],
 "cleanup_errors":[]}
```

`results` holds exactly fourteen entries in the order of the table, whatever happened. `comparison` is `lt`, `le` or `ge`. `measured` is `null` when there is no measurement. `hub.version` is the document `GET /version` returned. The token appears nowhere in the report, and text taken from a hub response is cut to 200 bytes.

### End-to-end flows

**A host with an old git.** An operator starts `parleyd` on a host whose `git` is 2.30. `parleyd` loads its configuration, opens its data, runs `git --version`, writes one error line saying that git 2.30 is too old and that 2.38 is needed, and exits 1 without listening. The operator installs a newer `git` and starts `parleyd` again; it logs `git version checked`, runs the other start hooks, listens, and answers `GET /readyz` with 200.

**An upgrade.** An operator stops the hub of the previous release and starts the new `parleyd` on the same data. `parleyd` opens the stores, applies the schema steps the data does not record, runs its start hooks and listens. The operator reads `GET /readyz` and receives 200; the repositories are as they were. At the next restart `parleyd` applies no step.

**Backup under load, then restore.** While agents commit and push, an operator runs `parleyd backup <directory>`; `parleyd` writes the snapshot and the work of the agents goes on without an error. The operator copies the snapshot to a new host and starts `parleyd` there; it applies no step, runs its start hooks on the restored data, listens and answers `GET /readyz` with 200. The stores pass their integrity check and stock `git` reads every repository.

**A performance run.** An operator sets `PARLEY_PERF_URL`, the token and the workspace and runs the performance test. The harness reads `GET /version` from `parleyd`, runs the fourteen scenarios against it one after the other, deletes what it created, and writes the report. The operator reads, per target, the measured value and the verdict.

## Design Decisions

1. **Project decisions relied on.** Go; the server needs the `git` command, 2.38 or later, run as a subprocess; the stores are embedded SQLite through `modernc.org/sqlite` behind `internal/store`; HTTP is the standard library's; tests use the standard `testing` package, table-driven, with `net/http/httptest` and `t.TempDir()`; `test/e2e` tests start a hub in-process through the run function of `internal/hub`.
2. **The git check is the first start hook.** The PRD says "checked at start" and not where. Package 03's start hooks already give a failing start its exit status and its one error line, so the check is a hook named `git-version` that the hub's composition registers before every other. A consequence: runs that exit before the hooks (`--help`, `backup`, the bootstrap runs) do not check, and need no `git`.
3. **Only major and minor are compared**, and whatever follows them is ignored, because vendors append their own suffixes. The time limit is 10 seconds. `git` is found on the `PATH` of the hub's environment lookup, which lets a test place a script named `git` first on that `PATH`.
4. **Recorded data is an archive, not a directory.** A bare repository holds empty directories that git does not track, so a recorded data directory is kept as one `.tar.gz` per release and unpacked by the test.
5. **What a recording holds.** A bootstrapped, cleanly stopped hub with one repository. The PRD does not say what "the data of the previous release" must contain; this is the smallest data that has every table of the release, an admin token hash and a repository. Seeding a recording with workspaces, changes and sessions through the REST API is later work.
6. **Every recorded archive is tested, not only the previous release's.** The PRD requires the previous release; keeping older archives passing costs nothing until one fails, and then deleting it is a visible decision.
7. **The compatibility rule is a function of the upgrade package**, so that a renamed or removed step fails with the step's name instead of with whatever the step would do when applied a second time. Reading a store's applied steps is added to `internal/store` as a read-only listing.
8. **Level names.** `TRACE`, `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARN`, `ERROR`, the spelling package 03's tests already expect for `ERROR`. `time` is UTC so that logs of hosts in different zones sort together.
9. **The request id reaches a line through the context.** Code logs with the request's context; the logger adds `request_id` from the id package 02 puts there. Code that logs without a context gets no id; the PRD's "carry the request id" is read as "where there is a request".
10. **The query string is left out of the access log** altogether instead of being scrubbed, because a value in it that the scrubber does not know (a forge webhook token) would pass.
11. **Restore is a copy, not a command.** The PRD defines `parleyd backup` and no counterpart. The two stores of a snapshot are copied one after the other, so they need not show the same instant; a hub starts on them regardless, and the feature packages' start hooks reconcile.
12. **Images.** The base image is the implementer's choice among those whose packaged `git` is 2.38 or later; the hub image test fails otherwise, because the hub in it refuses to start. User id 10001 for the hub and 1000 for the sandbox image, port 8080, the volume `/var/lib/parley` and the image names `parley-hub` and `parley-sandbox` are this package's choices; the PRD names none.
13. **The config dir is on the data volume.** The bootstrap writes the admin token file into the config dir and the hub refuses to start while the file exists (PLAT-FR-003). A read-only ConfigMap directory cannot hold that file and a container's own filesystem loses it at the next restart, so the image puts the config dir on the volume and the manifests mount only the file `config.toml` into it.
14. **No bootstrap manifest (a known gap of the source PRD).** The Deployment runs `parleyd` with no flags; a hub that is not bootstrapped serves without an admin token. How an operator runs `parleyd --admin-email` once on the volume and takes the token file is a cluster procedure NFR-006 does not list; it is left out. The gap is recorded here and no behaviour is added for it.
15. **`Recreate`, one replica, 40 seconds.** A rolling update would start a second hub on the same data, which NFR-001 forbids. 40 seconds is the hub's 30-second bound plus a margin.
16. **Image tests and the performance test are gated by environment variables, not build tags**, so they are compiled and linted in every run and skipped unless asked for. Manifests are checked by parsing them; no cluster is needed.
17. **The harness is a black-box HTTP client of a hub the operator names.** The targets are stated for a host of 8 cores and 32 GB with repositories of up to 5 GB; only the operator can provide that hub and that workspace. The harness uses `net/http` directly and imports no server code. Its exact requests are those of the packages that own the routes.
18. **Samples and deadlines** (50, 200, 20, 120, 16, 100, 5; 10 and 60 minutes) are this package's choices. `sandbox_exec` reports the whole request duration of `true` as an upper bound of the overhead, because a client cannot separate the hub's share. `event_latency` and `sandbox_ready` report the largest sample, since their targets say "within".
19. **Capacity scenarios stop at the hub's refusal and report the count (a known gap of the source PRD).** The default limits (200 forks per workspace, 20 sandboxes per user) are below two of the capacity targets; whether the operator lists 25 workspaces or raises a limit is theirs to decide, and the report shows what was reached. The source PRD's defaults and targets disagree; this package changes neither.
20. **Package 02 is added to the dependencies** beside the plan's 03: the request id a log line must carry is created there, and the access-log line is written by its `internal/server/accesslog.go`. Dropping the query string from `path` is package 02's criterion (REQ-8.5 there: `path` is the URL path without the query string); this package relies on package 02 for that point, edits nothing in that file, and only confirms it in its own log tests.
21. **Profile: full**, with four execution paths.

## Dependencies

- Package 03 server_lifecycle_and_configuration (draft): the run function, start hooks, the stores and schema steps, the logger and scrubber, `parleyd backup`, the configuration loader.
- Package 02 http_api_conventions (draft): the request id in the request's context and the access-log line.
- External: a container engine (`docker` or a compatible command) for the image tests only; a running hub for the performance test only.

## Verified External API

`gopkg.in/yaml.v3` v3.0.1, read in the module cache (`yaml.go`); used only by the manifest test:

- `func Unmarshal(in []byte, out interface{}) (err error)`
- `func NewDecoder(r io.Reader) *Decoder`
- `func (dec *Decoder) Decode(v interface{}) (err error)`

`log/slog`, `archive/tar`, `compress/gzip` and `os/exec` are the standard library's.

## Glossary

- **Hub**: The `parleyd` server.
- **Workspace**: A repository the hub holds, identified by its `slug`. Either a registered repository or a task fork.
- **Task fork (fork)**: A workspace created from another workspace (its parent) for one task. It shares history with the parent, has its own branches and expires: after 7 days by default, or 24 hours after all its changes have landed or been abandoned.
- **Change**: The unit of work: a proposal to add the commits of a source branch to a target branch, with a number, a title, an intent, versions and a state.
- **Landing**: Adding a change's commits to its target branch: a server-side rebase followed by a compare-and-swap of the target ref.
- **Land attempt**: One request to land a change (or a stack), with its outcome.
- **Sandbox**: An isolated environment in which an agent runs, attached to a workspace (normally a task fork) and started with it checked out. It runs on OpenShell; the hub controls it (§13).
- **Profile**: The operator's template for a sandbox, defined in configuration: image, resources, time limits, base policy, credentials and the secrets it exposes.
- **Hub event**: A record of something the hub did (`parley.*` types), with a sequence number. Hub events form the audit log and the event stream.
- **Snapshot**: The directory `parleyd backup` writes: the two stores and the workspace root.
- **Recorded data**: An archive under `test/upgrade/testdata/` holding the data directory a release wrote, with its manifest.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Git version check at start

**Rationale:** A hub on a host without a usable git fails at the first clone or push; it is cheaper to refuse the start and say why.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] WHEN parleyd starts to serve and git on the PATH of its environment answers git --version with a first line git version <major>.<minor> followed by anything, where (major, minor) is at least (2, 38), THE parleyd SHALL run git --version exactly once as the start hook git-version, before every other registered start hook, accept the version, and write one info log line with msg 'git version checked' and the member git_version holding the text after 'git version ' up to the first space
   → the hub goes on to listen; stderr holds exactly one line with msg 'git version checked', and it precedes the first effect of every other start hook; git_version is for example '2.39.3' for the output 'git version 2.39.3 (Apple Git-146)'
   Check: integration
   - setup: a temporary directory first on the PATH of the hub's environment lookup, holding an executable script named git that the test writes
   - setup: a temporary working directory with a config.toml setting bind 127.0.0.1 and port 0
   ```
   in internal/hub/gitcheck_test.go: the script prints 'git version 2.39.3 (Apple Git-146)' and appends a line to a counter file; register a start hook h that appends 'h' to a shared log and records whether the 'git version checked' line is already on stderr; run the hub; wait for the listening line; assert lines(counter file) == 1; assert h saw the line; rec = json(the line); assert rec.level == 'INFO' and rec.git_version == '2.39.3'; and once with the real git of the test host: assert the hub listens
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] THE parleyd SHALL for any first line of the output of git --version, read the version as the two decimal numbers that follow 'git version ' separated by a dot, ignore everything after the minor number, and accept exactly the versions whose (major, minor) is at least (2, 38)
   → the parsing function returns (major, minor, the version text up to the first space) or an error; the comparison accepts 2.38, 2.38.0, 2.45.1.windows.1, 2.50.0-rc1, 2.100.0 and 3.0, and refuses 2.37.7, 2.9.5 and 1.9
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/gitrepo/version_test.go, a table of (line, want major, want minor, want text, accepted): ('git version 2.38.0', 2, 38, '2.38.0', true), ('git version 2.38', 2, 38, '2.38', true), ('git version 2.39.3 (Apple Git-146)', 2, 39, '2.39.3', true), ('git version 2.45.1.windows.1', 2, 45, '2.45.1.windows.1', true), ('git version 2.50.0-rc1', 2, 50, '2.50.0-rc1', true), ('git version 2.100.0', 2, 100, '2.100.0', true), ('git version 3.0', 3, 0, '3.0', true), ('git version 2.37.7', 2, 37, '2.37.7', false), ('git version 2.9.5', 2, 9, '2.9.5', false), ('git version 1.9', 1, 9, '1.9', false): v, err = gitrepo.ParseVersion(line); assert err == nil; assert v.Major == major and v.Minor == minor and v.Text == text; assert v.AtLeast(2, 38) == accepted; and a table of lines that return an error: '', 'git version', 'git version two', 'git version 2', 'hg version 2.40', 'version 2.40.0'
   ```
1. [REQ-1.3] IF parleyd starts to serve and no executable named git is on the PATH of its environment, THEN THE parleyd SHALL stop the start in the git-version hook without calling any later start hook and without listening
   → exit status 1; stderr holds exactly one non-empty line, a JSON object at level ERROR whose text contains 'git not found on PATH; parleyd needs git 2.38 or later'; no line with msg 'listening'; a start hook registered by another package is not called
   Check: integration
   - setup: a temporary working directory with a valid config.toml; the PATH of the hub's environment lookup is set by each table row
   ```
   in internal/hub/gitcheck_test.go, a table of (arrangement of the PATH, text the error line must contain): (a PATH of one empty directory, 'git not found on PATH; parleyd needs git 2.38 or later'), (script prints 'git version 2.30.2', 'git 2.30.2 is too old; parleyd needs git 2.38 or later'), (script prints 'git version 2.37.7', 'git 2.37.7 is too old'), (script prints 'gti 2.40', 'cannot read the git version from "gti 2.40"'), (script exits 3 without output, 'git --version failed: exit status 3'): register a start hook h that sets a flag; code = hub.Run(ctx, opts); assert code == 1; lines = nonEmptyLines(stderr); assert len(lines) == 1; assert json(lines[0]).level == 'ERROR'; assert contains(lines[0], text); assert not contains(stderr, 'listening'); assert h's flag is unset
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] IF parleyd starts to serve and git --version reports a version whose (major, minor) is below (2, 38), THEN THE parleyd SHALL stop the start in the git-version hook, naming the version that was found
   → exit status 1; one JSON error line whose text contains 'git <found> is too old; parleyd needs git 2.38 or later', where <found> is the version text git printed; no listening line
   Check: same as REQ-1.3
1. [REQ-1.5] IF the first line of the output of git --version does not have the form git version <major>.<minor>, or git --version exits with a status other than 0, or it has not answered after 10 seconds, THEN THE parleyd SHALL return an error from the version check, kill the git process when the time limit passed, and stop the start with that error
   → the check returns an error whose text is 'cannot read the git version from "<first line cut to 100 bytes>"', 'git --version failed: exit status <n>' or 'git --version failed: no answer within <limit>'; with a time limit the check returns no later than 2 seconds after the limit and the process it started no longer runs; at start the exit status is 1 with one JSON error line holding that text
   Check: unit
   - setup: a temporary directory with an executable script named git, and a path lookup that resolves git to it
   ```
   in internal/gitrepo/version_test.go, with the script as git: (a) script prints a first line of 300 'x' characters: _, err = gitrepo.CheckVersion(ctx, lookPath, 10*time.Second); assert contains(err.Error(), 'cannot read the git version from "' + 100 'x' characters + '"'); (b) script exits 3: assert contains(err.Error(), 'git --version failed: exit status 3'); (c) script writes its process id to a file and sleeps 60 seconds: start = now; _, err = gitrepo.CheckVersion(ctx, lookPath, 200*time.Millisecond); assert contains(err.Error(), 'no answer within 200ms'); assert now - start < 2200 ms; assert the process with the recorded id no longer exists
   ```
1. [REQ-1.6] WHEN parleyd is run as parleyd --help, with a usage error, as parleyd backup <directory>, or as a bootstrap run that writes the admin token and exits (--admin-email on a hub with no admin token hash, or --reset-admin-token), THE parleyd SHALL complete the run without running git
   → on a PATH that holds no git the run ends as it does on a host with git: exit status 0 for --help, the backup and the bootstrap runs, 2 for the usage error; stderr holds no text 'git not found'
   Check: integration
   - setup: a temporary working directory with a valid config.toml
   ```
   in internal/hub/gitcheck_test.go, a table of (arguments, want exit status) run with a PATH of one empty directory: (['--help'], 0), (['--no-such-flag'], 2), (['--admin-email=a@x'] on a new data directory, 0), (['--reset-admin-token'], 0), (['backup', target] on the data directory the bootstrap row created, 0): code = hub.Run(ctx, opts); assert code == want; assert not contains(stderr, 'git not found')
   ```

### REQ-2: A newer binary opens the previous release's data

**Rationale:** An upgrade must be a restart, not a migration project (NFR-003).

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] WHEN a person runs go run ./test/upgrade/record <name> with a name that matches ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,62}$ and no archive of that name exists, THE upgrade recorder SHALL start a hub in a temporary directory with --admin-email, start it again to serve, create the bare repository fixture.git with one commit on main under its workspace root, stop it with a clean shutdown, and write test/upgrade/testdata/<name>.tar.gz holding the data directory and manifest.json
   → exit status 0; stdout is the archive's path and a newline; the archive holds the transactional store, analytics.db, the workspace root with fixture.git, and manifest.json with release == <name>, recorded_at, steps.transactional and steps.analytical (the applied schema steps of each store in order of application), admin_token_sha256 (64 lowercase hex characters, the stored hash) and repositories == [{path: 'fixture.git', refs: {'refs/heads/main': <40 hex>}}]; the temporary directory is removed
   Check: integration
   - setup: record.Run takes the output directory as a parameter; the command passes test/upgrade/testdata
   ```
   in test/upgrade/record/record_test.go: out = t.TempDir(); code = record.Run(ctx, ['r1'], out, stdout, stderr); assert code == 0; assert stdout == out + '/r1.tar.gz\n'; unpack the archive into d; m = json(d/manifest.json); assert m.release == 'r1'; assert m.steps.transactional == store.AppliedSteps(open d's transactional store) and likewise analytical; assert len(m.admin_token_sha256) == 64; assert m.repositories[0].path == 'fixture.git'; assert exec('git', '-C', d/<workspace root>/fixture.git, 'rev-parse', 'refs/heads/main') == m.repositories[0].refs['refs/heads/main']
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] IF the name given to the recorder does not match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,62}$, no name or more than one is given, or test/upgrade/testdata/<name>.tar.gz already exists, THEN THE upgrade recorder SHALL refuse without starting a hub and without writing or changing any file
   → exit status 1; stdout is empty; stderr holds one line that names the cause (the name and the pattern, or the existing archive's path); the output directory's listing and the bytes of an existing archive are unchanged
   Check: unit
   ```
   in test/upgrade/record/record_test.go, a table of argument lists: [], ['a', 'b'], ['Upper'], ['-x'], ['a/b'], [65 characters 'a'], and ['r1'] with out/r1.tar.gz already holding the bytes 'old': code = record.Run(ctx, args, out, stdout, stderr); assert code == 1; assert stdout == ''; assert len(nonEmptyLines(stderr)) == 1; assert listDir(out) is unchanged; in the last row assert read(out/r1.tar.gz) == 'old' and contains(stderr, 'r1.tar.gz')
   ```
1. [REQ-2.3] WHEN parleyd is started with no flags on the unpacked data of a recorded archive under test/upgrade/testdata, THE parleyd SHALL apply every registered schema step that the data does not record, apply no recorded step again, run the start hooks, listen, and keep what the data held
   → the listening line is logged and GET /readyz answers 200; in each store the list of applied steps begins with the manifest's list for that store in the same order and holds every registered step of that store; the stored admin token hash equals the manifest's admin_token_sha256; for each repository of the manifest git fsck exits 0 and each ref resolves to the manifest's commit id; on SIGTERM the exit status is 0
   Check: integration
   - setup: test/upgrade/testdata holds at least baseline.tar.gz, recorded by the recorder when this package was implemented
   ```
   in test/upgrade/upgrade_test.go, one subtest per archive in testdata (the test fails when there is none): unpack into d; write config.toml with database.path and workspace.path inside d, bind 127.0.0.1, port 0; run the hub; rec = json(listening line); assert get('http://' + rec.addr + '/readyz').status == 200; cancel; assert exit status == 0; for each store: applied = store.AppliedSteps(store); assert applied[0:len(m.steps[store])] == m.steps[store]; assert set(applied) == set(names of the registered steps of that store); assert the admin token hash read through internal/identity == m.admin_token_sha256; for r in m.repositories: assert exec('git', '-C', d/workspaces/r.path, 'fsck').code == 0; for ref, sha in r.refs: assert exec('git', '-C', ..., 'rev-parse', ref) == sha
   ```
1. [REQ-2.4] WHEN parleyd is started a second time on data it has already brought to the current schema, THE parleyd SHALL apply no schema step and leave the record of applied steps of both stores as it was
   → the lists of applied steps of both stores are equal before and after the second start; the hub listens and answers GET /readyz with 200
   Check: same as PATH-2
1. [REQ-2.5] THE upgrade test SHALL for any list of recorded step names and any list of registered step names, report the pair as compatible exactly when every recorded name is registered and the recorded names appear among the registered ones in the same relative order, and otherwise name the first recorded step that breaks the rule
   → upgrade.Compatible(recorded, registered) returns nil for a compatible pair and otherwise an error whose text contains the step's name and 'not registered' or 'out of order'; the upgrade test calls it for both stores of every archive before it starts the hub and fails with that text
   Check: unit
   ```
   in test/upgrade/compat_test.go, a table of (recorded, registered, want): ([], [], nil), ([], ['a'], nil), (['a', 'b'], ['a', 'b', 'c'], nil), (['a', 'c'], ['a', 'b', 'c'], nil), (['a', 'b'], ['a'], error containing 'b' and 'not registered'), (['a', 'b'], ['a', 'b2'], 'b' and 'not registered'), (['a', 'b'], ['b', 'a'], 'b' and 'out of order'), (['a'], [], 'a' and 'not registered'): err = upgrade.Compatible(recorded, registered); assert (err == nil) == (want == nil); where want is an error assert contains(err.Error(), each expected text)
   ```

### REQ-3: Structured logging rules

**Rationale:** Logs are read by machines and kept by third parties: each line must parse, must be attributable to a request, and must never carry a credential (NFR-042).

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] THE parleyd SHALL for any line it logs, write exactly one line of text that is one JSON object with the members time (an RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC ending in Z), level (one of TRACE, DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR) and msg (a string)
   → a line logged at the trace level has level 'TRACE'; a message or value that contains a line break is written with the break escaped, so the output has exactly one newline per logged line
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/hub/logging_test.go, beside the level-filter test: log = hub.NewLogger(buffer, 'trace', scrubber) with a clock fixed at 2026-03-04T05:06:07+02:00; emit one line at each of the five levels, the last with msg 'two\nlines' and an attribute 'v' = 'a\nb'; assert count(buffer, '\n') == 5; for each line: rec = json(line); assert rec.time ends with 'Z' and parses as RFC 3339 to the instant 2026-03-04T03:06:07Z; assert [rec.level for each line] == ['TRACE', 'DEBUG', 'INFO', 'WARN', 'ERROR']; assert json(last line).msg == 'two\nlines'
   ```
1. [REQ-3.2] WHEN code logs a line with the context of a request that the HTTP server is handling, THE parleyd SHALL add the member request_id to the line, equal to the request id of that request
   → the line's request_id equals the X-Request-ID header of the request's response, for a line written by a handler and for a line written by code the handler calls with the request's context; a line logged with a context that belongs to no request, or without a context, has no request_id member
   Check: integration
   - setup: the request id middleware of package 02 is installed
   ```
   in internal/hub/logging_test.go: build the HTTP server of internal/server with the hub's logger and a test route whose handler logs 'in handler' with r.Context() and calls a function that logs 'deeper' with the same context; resp = get(route); id = resp.header['X-Request-ID']; assert json(line 'in handler').request_id == id; assert json(line 'deeper').request_id == id; send a second request and assert its lines carry the second response's id; log.InfoContext(context.Background(), 'background'); log.Info('no context'); assert 'request_id' not in json(line 'background'); assert 'request_id' not in json(line 'no context')
   ```
1. [REQ-3.3] WHEN a line is logged with an attribute whose value is an error, a nested group of attributes, a list, a map, a byte slice or a value that is rendered as text, THE parleyd SHALL render the value and pass every string in the rendering through the scrubber before the line is written, rendering an error as its message, and write numbers, booleans and durations unchanged
   → no string anywhere in the line holds a registered secret value, a credential in one of the hub's formats or user information in a URL; each is replaced by [redacted] or the URL without user information, as for a string attribute; attribute keys are unchanged
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/hub/logging_test.go, beside the scrubbing test: s = scrub.New(); s.Add('hunter2'); log = hub.NewLogger(buffer, 'info', s); a table of attribute values: errors.New('auth hunter2 failed'), fmt.Errorf('wrap: %w', errors.New('https://u:hunter2@h/r.git')), slog.Group('g', 'inner', 'hunter2', 'n', 7), ['a', 'hunter2'], {'k': 'hunter2'}, []byte('hunter2'), a value whose String method returns 'tok hunter2', a generated personal access token inside a struct field: log.Info('m', 'v', value, 'count', 3, 'ok', true); assert not contains(line, 'hunter2'); assert not contains(line, the token); assert contains(line, '[redacted]') or (for the URL row) contains(line, 'https://h/r.git'); rec = json(line); assert rec.count == 3 and rec.ok == true; for the first row assert rec.v == 'auth [redacted] failed'
   ```
1. [REQ-3.4] THE parleyd SHALL for any request, write the path member of its access-log line as the path of the request's URL without the query string
   → a request to /version?token=s3cr3t&x=1 gives an access-log line whose path is '/version' and which contains neither 's3cr3t' nor '?'
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/server/headers_test.go, beside the access-log test: a table of request targets ('/version?token=s3cr3t&x=1', '/api/v1/none?a=b', '/version'): send the request through the server with a buffer as log; rec = json(the access-log line); assert rec.path == the target up to but excluding '?'; assert not contains(line, 's3cr3t'); assert not contains(line, '?')
   ```
1. [REQ-3.5] IF a write of a log line to stderr returns an error, THEN THE parleyd SHALL drop the line and go on, without failing the request that caused the line and without stopping the process
   → the request is answered with the status and body it has when logging works; later requests are answered; the hub's exit status at a later SIGTERM is 0
   Check: integration
   - setup: a temporary working directory with a valid config.toml and [logging].level trace
   ```
   in internal/hub/logging_test.go: run the hub with a stderr writer that returns an error for every write after the listening line; r1 = get('/version'); assert r1.status == 200 and r1.json.version != ''; r2 = get('/api/v1/no-such-route'); assert r2.status == 404; cancel; assert exit status == 0
   ```
1. [REQ-3.6] THE parleyd SHALL for any run at level trace in which requests carry secrets in an Authorization Bearer header, an Authorization Basic header, a Cookie header, a JSON body and a query parameter, write a log in which every line is a JSON object with time, level and msg, every access-log line carries the request_id of its response, and none of those secrets appears
   → every non-empty line of stderr parses as a JSON object with the three members; for each response the log holds an access-log line whose request_id equals its X-Request-ID; no line contains any of the five marker secrets, neither as sent nor base64-encoded
   Check: integration
   - setup: an in-process hub with [logging].level trace and log_health_probes true, started through the run function with a buffer as stderr
   ```
   in test/e2e/logging_test.go: five distinct random markers of 24 characters; send to the running hub: GET /api/v1/user with 'Authorization: Bearer ' + m1; GET /git/acme/app.git/info/refs?service=git-upload-pack with Basic auth user 'x' and password m2; GET /version with 'Cookie: session=' + m3; POST /api/v1/no-such-route with content type application/json and body {'secret': m4}; GET /healthz?token=m5; collect each response's X-Request-ID; stop the hub; for line in nonEmptyLines(stderr): rec = json(line); assert rec.time != '' and rec.level != '' and rec.msg is a string; for each collected id: assert at least one line has the members method, path and status and request_id == id; for m in markers: assert not contains(stderr, m); assert not contains(stderr, base64('x:' + m2))
   ```

### REQ-4: Restore of a backup taken under load

**Rationale:** A backup is worth what its restore is worth; NFR-007 promises that a hub started on a restored snapshot starts cleanly.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-4.1] WHEN an operator copies a snapshot written by parleyd backup to a new place (the transactional store to [database].path, analytics.db beside it, the workspace directory to [workspace].path) and starts parleyd there with no flags, THE parleyd SHALL open the copied stores without applying a schema step, run every registered start hook to completion with the restored data open, listen, and accept new work
   → the listening line is logged and GET /readyz answers 200; a start hook registered by the test is called once before the listener is bound and reads the restored rows; the stored admin token hash equals the source hub's; a transaction on the restored transactional store commits, and git push of a new commit to a restored repository exits 0; every file of the snapshot directory that was copied from has the same content hash as before the start
   Check: integration
   - setup: a bootstrapped source hub with a schema step creating table a with 100 committed rows and one bare repository r.git with two commits, backed up with parleyd backup into a snapshot directory
   ```

   → the hub started on the copy logs the listening line and answers GET /readyz with 200; PRAGMA integrity_check answers ok on each restored store; the row count of the load table is a multiple of 10; for each restored repository git fsck exits 0, its ref refs/heads/main resolves to a commit that is the source repository's commit of that ref at the end of the load or an ancestor of it, and every commit pushed before the backup started is an ancestor of the restored ref or equal to it

   ```

   → the check passes for the reference image and, when PARLEY_SANDBOX_IMAGE is set, is also run against that image; for an image without git it fails with a message that contains the image reference and 'git'

   → in a container of the image: git --version prints a version of at least 2.38; /bin/sh -c true exits 0; parley version exits 0 and prints a JSON document whose cli.version is the build argument VERSION, also with PARLEY_ENDPOINT_URL set to an address nothing listens on; command -v parleyd exits with a status other than 0; a file of CA certificates exists and is not empty

### REQ-7: Kubernetes manifests

**Rationale:** NFR-006 lists manifests with one replica and a persistent volume claim; NFR-001 forbids a second replica, also during an update.

   → the five files each decode to one object of the named kind and name; the Deployment's spec.replicas is 1 and spec.strategy.type is 'Recreate'; its only container's image is a parley-hub reference and it has no command or args, so the image's entry point runs with no flags

   → the claim has the access mode ReadWriteOnce alone, requests 20Gi of storage and names no storage class; the container has a volume mount of the claim's volume at /var/lib/parley and a volume mount of the ConfigMap's volume at /var/lib/parley/config/config.toml with subPath config.toml; the pod's securityContext has runAsUser 10001, runAsNonRoot true and fsGroup 10001

### REQ-9: Performance scenarios

**Rationale:** Each row of the table of §15.4 needs one defined way of being measured, or two runs cannot be compared.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-9.1] THE performance harness SHALL run the scenarios fork_create (50 forks created one after the other), file_read (200 reads, alternately a file and a tree), commit_create (50 commits of 100 files each on a fork) and sandbox_exec (50 execs of the command true in one sandbox), measure the duration of each request from sending it to reading the end of its response, and report the p95 in milliseconds against the targets under 1000, under 100, under 500 and under 200
   → the results carry samples 50, 200, 50 and 50, target {lt, 1000 | 100 | 500 | 200, ms} and measured equal to the p95 of the durations; every request carries Authorization: Bearer <token>; file_read sends 100 requests to …/scm/file and 100 to …/scm/tree; each commit request holds 100 file operations
   Check: unit
   - setup: a stub hub built with net/http/httptest that answers GET /version and the scenario routes as each row says
   ```
   in test/perf/scenarios_test.go: the stub delays each fork response by 20 ms and counts requests per route, checking the Authorization header and the number of file operations in each commit body; rep = perf.Run(ctx, cfg with SandboxProfile 'agent'); for (name, samples, value) in {('fork_create', 50, 1000), ('file_read', 200, 100), ('commit_create', 50, 500), ('sandbox_exec', 50, 200)}: r = result(name); assert r.samples == samples; assert r.target == {comparison: 'lt', value: value, unit: 'ms'}; assert r.status == 'met'; assert result('fork_create').measured >= 20; assert stub count of scm/file == 100 and of scm/tree == 100; assert every commit body held 100 operations; assert every request carried the bearer token; and with the fork route delayed by 1100 ms for 5 of the 50 requests: assert result('fork_create').status == 'missed'
   ```
1. [REQ-9.2] THE performance harness SHALL run the scenario land (20 changes of 20 commits each with disjoint files, landed one at a time, measuring the time from the land request to the success of its land attempt; p95 in milliseconds, target under 2000), the scenario land_throughput (120 one-commit changes with disjoint files landed on one target branch with at most 8 land requests in flight; changes landed times 60 divided by the seconds elapsed, target at least 60) and the scenario land_concurrency (16 land requests for 16 non-conflicting changes sent at the same time; the number of land attempts that did not end in success, target at most 0)
   → land has samples 20 and target {lt, 2000, ms}; land_throughput has samples 120 and target {ge, 60, per_minute}, and the stub never sees more than 8 land requests of it in flight; land_concurrency has samples 16 and target {le, 0, count}, and its measured value is the number of attempts whose final state is not success; a land attempt that fails is counted, not treated as a request error
   Check: unit
   - setup: a stub hub built with net/http/httptest that answers GET /version and the scenario routes as each row says
   ```
   in test/perf/scenarios_test.go: the stub answers land requests after 50 ms, tracks the largest number in flight per scenario (told apart by the change numbers it handed out), and lets 2 of the 16 attempts of land_concurrency end as failed: rep = perf.Run(ctx, cfg); l = result('land'); assert l.samples == 20 and l.target == {comparison: 'lt', value: 2000, unit: 'ms'} and l.status == 'met'; t = result('land_throughput'); assert t.samples == 120 and t.target == {comparison: 'ge', value: 60, unit: 'per_minute'}; assert stub.maxInFlight('land_throughput') <= 8; assert t.measured == 120 * 60 / elapsed seconds within 10 percent; c = result('land_concurrency'); assert c.measured == 2 and c.status == 'missed'; assert stub.maxInFlight('land_concurrency') == 16
   ```
1. [REQ-9.3] THE performance harness SHALL run the scenario mergeability (with 100 open changes, move the target branch by landing one more change and measure the seconds until none of the 100 reports mergeable unknown, target at most 60) and the scenario event_latency (with one subscriber on GET /events, create 50 commits one after the other and measure, for each, the time from the commit's response to the arrival of its event; the largest in milliseconds, target at most 1000)
   → mergeability has samples 100 and target {le, 60, s}; it polls the changes no faster than once per second and ends in error with 'deadline exceeded' when a change still reports unknown at the scenario's deadline; event_latency has samples 50 and target {le, 1000, ms}; an event that arrives before its commit's response counts as 0; an event that has not arrived 10 seconds after its response ends the scenario in error
   Check: unit
   - setup: a stub hub built with net/http/httptest that answers GET /version and the scenario routes as each row says
   ```
   in test/perf/scenarios_test.go: the stub reports mergeable 'unknown' for the 100 changes until 2 s after the extra land and 'clean' afterwards, and sends each commit's event on the open GET /events stream 30 ms after the commit's response: rep = perf.Run(ctx, cfg); m = result('mergeability'); assert m.samples == 100 and m.target == {comparison: 'le', value: 60, unit: 's'}; assert 2 <= m.measured < 5 and m.status == 'met'; e = result('event_latency'); assert e.samples == 50 and e.target == {comparison: 'le', value: 1000, unit: 'ms'}; assert 30 <= e.measured < 1000; and with the stub withholding the event of the 10th commit and the event wait set to 200 ms through the configuration: assert result('event_latency').status == 'error'
   ```
1. [REQ-9.4] WHERE PARLEY_PERF_CAPACITY is 1, THE performance harness SHALL run the capacity scenarios active_forks (forks created over all listed workspaces until 5,000 exist), open_changes (changes opened in the first workspace until 2,000 are open), event_streams (GET /events connections opened until 500 are open) and, with a sandbox profile set, sandboxes_running (sandboxes created until 200 are provisioning or ready), ending each when its count is reached or the hub refuses a creation, and report the count reached against the targets at least 5000, 2000, 500 and 200
   → each result has target {ge, the count, count} and measured equal to the number that existed at once; a refusal by the hub (a status of 400 or more on the creating request) ends the scenario with status met or missed by the count, not error, and a detail that holds the refusal's error_type; active_forks moves to the next listed workspace when one refuses and ends when every listed workspace has refused
   Check: unit
   - setup: a stub hub built with net/http/httptest that answers GET /version and the scenario routes as each row says
   ```
   in test/perf/scenarios_test.go: cfg with Capacity true, SandboxProfile 'agent' and workspaces ['w1', 'w2']; the stub accepts 200 forks per workspace and then answers 409 with an error_type of its own, accepts 2,000 changes, accepts 500 event streams, and answers the 21st sandbox creation with 429 and error_type 'sandbox_capacity': rep = perf.Run(ctx, cfg); f = result('active_forks'); assert f.measured == 400 and f.status == 'missed' and f.target == {comparison: 'ge', value: 5000, unit: 'count'}; assert contains(f.detail, the stub's error_type); assert result('open_changes').measured == 2000 and result('open_changes').status == 'met'; assert result('event_streams').measured == 500 and result('event_streams').status == 'met'; s = result('sandboxes_running'); assert s.measured == 20 and s.status == 'missed' and contains(s.detail, 'sandbox_capacity')
   ```
1. [REQ-9.5] WHERE PARLEY_PERF_SANDBOX_PROFILE names a profile, THE performance harness SHALL run the scenario sandbox_ready: create 5 sandboxes of that profile one after the other, measure for each the time from the create response to the first read that shows state ready, and report the largest in seconds against the target at most 60
   → the result has samples 5 and target {le, 60, s}; every create request names the configured profile; a sandbox that reaches state failed ends the scenario in error with a detail that holds its state_reason
   Check: unit
   - setup: a stub hub built with net/http/httptest that answers GET /version and the scenario routes as each row says
   ```
   in test/perf/scenarios_test.go: the stub shows each sandbox as provisioning for 300 ms and then ready, and records the profile of each create request: rep = perf.Run(ctx, cfg with SandboxProfile 'agent'); r = result('sandbox_ready'); assert r.samples == 5 and r.target == {comparison: 'le', value: 60, unit: 's'}; assert 0.3 <= r.measured < 5 and r.status == 'met'; assert every recorded profile == 'agent'; and with the stub showing the third sandbox as failed with state_reason 'image_pull': assert result('sandbox_ready').status == 'error' and contains(result('sandbox_ready').detail, 'image_pull')
   ```
1. [REQ-9.6] THE performance harness SHALL for any scenario and any verdict, delete the forks and sandboxes the scenario created and close the connections it opened when the scenario ends, create every change against a target branch perf/<run id> of its own, and never move a workspace's default branch
   → after a run the stub holds no fork and no sandbox the harness created and no open event stream, also for a scenario that ended in error; no land request and no commit request named the default branch as its target; a clean-up request that is answered with a status of 400 or more adds an entry with its method, path and status to cleanup_errors and changes no result's status
   Check: unit
   - setup: a stub hub built with net/http/httptest that answers GET /version and the scenario routes as each row says
   ```
   in test/perf/scenarios_test.go: the stub records every created fork and sandbox, every delete, every open stream and the target branch of every change; run once with every route succeeding, and once with the commit route answering 500 from its 10th request: after each run assert stub.liveForks() == 0 and stub.liveSandboxes() == 0 and stub.openStreams() == 0; assert every recorded target branch == 'perf/' + rep.run_id; then with the stub answering the first fork delete with 500: rep = run; assert len(rep.cleanup_errors) == 1 and contains(rep.cleanup_errors[0], 'DELETE') and contains(rep.cleanup_errors[0], '500'); assert result('fork_create').status == 'met'
   ```

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: An operator starts the hub on a host whose git is too old, then on one that has a usable git

1. **operator** starts parleyd with no flags on a host whose git answers git version 2.30.2
2. **parleyd** loads its configuration, opens its data and runs git --version as the first start hook
3. **parleyd** writes one error line saying that git 2.30.2 is too old and that 2.38 or later is needed, and exits 1 without listening
4. **operator** puts a git of at least 2.38 on the PATH and starts parleyd again
5. **parleyd** logs 'git version checked', runs the other start hooks and listens
6. **operator** sends GET /readyz and receives 200

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the run function of internal/hub, internal/gitrepo running a real subprocess, the real git command of the test host in the second start, internal/store on real SQLite files, internal/server on a real TCP listener

**Setup:**

- a temporary working directory with a config.toml setting bind 127.0.0.1 and port 0
- a directory holding a script named git that prints 'git version 2.30.2'

**End state:**

- the first run returned 1 and its stderr holds one error line naming 2.30.2 and 2.38 and no listening line
- the second run logged 'git version checked' before the listening line and answers GET /readyz with 200
- the second run returns 0 after its context is cancelled

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/operations_test.go: code = run(ctx, [], env with PATH = scriptDir, dir, out, errb); assert code == 1; assert contains(errb, 'git 2.30.2 is too old') and not contains(errb, 'listening'); go run(ctx2, [], env with the test host's PATH, dir, out, errb2); rec = json(listening line of errb2); assert index(errb2, 'git version checked') < index(errb2, 'listening'); assert get('http://' + rec.addr + '/readyz').status == 200; cancel ctx2; assert exit status == 0
```

### PATH-2: An operator upgrades the hub by starting the new binary on the previous release's data

1. **operator** stops the hub of the previous release and starts the new parleyd on the same data directory with no flags
2. **parleyd** opens the stores and applies every registered schema step the data does not record, keeping the recorded ones
3. **parleyd** checks git, runs its start hooks and listens
4. **operator** sends GET /readyz and receives 200, and reads the repositories with stock git
5. **operator** restarts parleyd
6. **parleyd** applies no schema step, listens and answers GET /readyz with 200

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the run function of internal/hub with every schema step and start hook the binary registers, internal/store on the real SQLite files of a recorded archive, the git command on the recorded repository, internal/server on a real TCP listener

**Setup:**

- the archive test/upgrade/testdata/baseline.tar.gz unpacked into a temporary directory
- a config.toml pointing database.path and workspace.path into it, bind 127.0.0.1, port 0

**End state:**

- the first start listened and answered GET /readyz with 200
- after the first start each store's applied steps begin with the manifest's list
- the second start listened, answered GET /readyz with 200, and left both lists of applied steps equal to what they were after the first start
- git rev-parse refs/heads/main in fixture.git gives the manifest's commit id

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/upgrade/upgrade_test.go: start the hub on the unpacked data; assert readyz 200; stop it; a1 = store.AppliedSteps of both stores; assert a1 begins with the manifest's lists; start it again; assert readyz 200; stop it; a2 = store.AppliedSteps of both stores; assert a2 == a1; assert exec('git', '-C', d/workspaces/fixture.git, 'rev-parse', 'refs/heads/main') == manifest.repositories[0].refs['refs/heads/main']
```

### PATH-3: An operator backs up a hub under load and restores the snapshot to a hub that starts cleanly

1. **agent** commits work to the hub and pushes to its repositories, continuously
2. **operator** runs parleyd backup <directory> while that work goes on
3. **parleyd** as the backup command, writes the snapshot of both stores and the repositories and exits 0, while the serving parleyd completes every commit and push
4. **operator** copies the snapshot to a new data directory and starts parleyd there with no flags
5. **parleyd** opens the restored stores, applies no schema step, runs its start hooks on the restored data and listens
6. **operator** sends GET /readyz and receives 200, and reads every restored repository with stock git

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the run function of internal/hub for the serving hub, the backup subcommand and the restored hub, internal/store on real SQLite files, written by concurrent writers while the backup reads, the git command pushing to real bare repositories during the backup, internal/server on real TCP listeners

**Setup:**

- a running in-process hub with a schema step creating a load table, four writers committing transactions of 10 rows, and two git clients each pushing commits to one bare repository under the workspace root

**End state:**

- the backup returned 0 and no writer and no push saw an error
- a hub started on a copy of the snapshot logged the listening line and answers GET /readyz with 200
- PRAGMA integrity_check answers ok on both restored stores and the load table's row count is a multiple of 10
- git fsck succeeds on both restored repositories and each restored head is the source's head or an ancestor of it

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/restore_test.go: start the load; code = run(ctx, ['backup', target], env, dir, out, errb); assert code == 0; stop the load and assert no writer and no push had an error; copy target into d2/data; go run(ctx2, [], env, d2, out, errb2); rec = json(listening line); assert get('http://' + rec.addr + '/readyz').status == 200; stop hub 2; for each store assert query('PRAGMA integrity_check') == 'ok'; assert count(load table) % 10 == 0; for each repository assert exec('git', '-C', restored, 'fsck').code == 0 and exec('git', '-C', source, 'merge-base', '--is-ancestor', restoredHead, sourceHead).code == 0
```

### PATH-4: An operator measures the performance targets against a running hub

1. **operator** sets PARLEY_PERF_URL, PARLEY_PERF_TOKEN and PARLEY_PERF_WORKSPACE and runs go test ./test/perf/ -run TestPerformanceTargets
2. **parleyd** answers GET /version with its build values
3. **operator** through the harness, sends the requests of the fourteen scenarios one scenario after the other
4. **parleyd** answers each request; a route it does not have is answered 404 with the error envelope
5. **operator** reads the report: fourteen results, each with its measured value and its verdict, and the test passes whatever the verdicts are

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the harness of test/perf with its real HTTP client, a real in-process hub started through the run function of internal/hub on a loopback listener, the report file on disk

**Setup:**

- a running in-process hub with whatever routes the binary has
- a configuration with the hub's URL, the token 'parley_perf_smoke_token', the workspace 'perf-smoke' and a report path in t.TempDir()

**End state:**

- perf.Run returned a nil error
- the report file holds hub.version equal to the hub's GET /version document and exactly fourteen results in the fixed order
- every result has one of the four statuses, and a scenario whose route the hub refused has status error with the refusing status in its detail
- the report does not contain the token

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/perf/run_test.go: start the hub in-process; cfg = {URL: 'http://' + addr, Token: 'parley_perf_smoke_token', Workspaces: ['perf-smoke'], ReportPath: tmp + '/r.json'}; rep, err = perf.Run(ctx, cfg); assert err == nil; doc = json(read(cfg.ReportPath)); assert doc.hub.version == get(addr + '/version').json; assert len(doc.results) == 14; for r in doc.results: assert r.status in {'met', 'missed', 'skipped', 'error'}; assert not contains(read(cfg.ReportPath), cfg.Token)
```

### 1. Refuse to serve without git 2.38 or later (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-1

**Steps:**

- 1.1 Add the behaviours of the version check to internal/gitrepo/version_test.go and internal/hub/gitcheck_test.go and confirm they fail; the tests place a script named git first on the PATH of the hub's environment lookup
- 1.2 Add version parsing to internal/gitrepo: read the two numbers after 'git version ', keep the text up to the first space, ignore the rest, and compare on major and minor only
- 1.3 Add the check itself: resolve git through a path lookup it is given, run git --version with a time limit it is given, kill the process when the limit passes, and return one of the four error texts of the PRD's table (not found, too old, cannot read, failed)
- 1.4 Register the check in the hub's composition as the start hook named git-version, ahead of every other start hook, with a limit of 10 seconds and the PATH of the hub's environment lookup; on success log one info line 'git version checked' with git_version
- 1.5 Confirm that the runs that end before the start hooks (--help, a usage error, backup, the bootstrap runs) still succeed on a PATH without git, changing nothing in them
- 1.6 Add the end-to-end test of the old-git start followed by the good start to test/e2e/operations_test.go

**Touches:**

### 9. Measure the latency and throughput targets (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-9.1, REQ-9.2, REQ-9.3, REQ-9.6

**Steps:**

- 9.1 Add the behaviours to test/perf/scenarios_test.go and extend the stub hub with the fork, source control, change, land, event and sandbox exec routes; confirm they fail. Take the request and response shapes of each route from the PRD section that owns it (docs/prd/04, 06, 07, 08, 13 and 14)
- 9.2 Add the set-up every scenario shares: a target branch perf/<run id> in the first workspace, never the default branch, and the record of every fork, sandbox and stream a scenario creates
- 9.3 Add the clean-up that runs when a scenario ends in any verdict: delete its forks and sandboxes, close its streams, and list each clean-up request answered with 400 or more in cleanup_errors with its method, path and status
- 9.4 Add fork_create, file_read, commit_create and sandbox_exec as request-duration scenarios with 50, 200, 50 and 50 samples; sandbox_exec is skipped without a sandbox profile
- 9.5 Add land (20 changes of 20 commits, one at a time, from the land request to the success of the land attempt), land_throughput (120 changes, at most 8 land requests in flight, landed times 60 over the seconds elapsed) and land_concurrency (16 land requests at once, counting the attempts that did not end in success as the measurement, not as request errors)
- 9.6 Add mergeability: 100 open changes, one more change landed to move the target, polling no faster than once per second until none reports unknown
- 9.7 Add event_latency: one subscriber on GET /events, 50 commits, the largest time from response to event, 0 for an event that came first, and error for an event that has not come after the event wait (10 seconds)
